question: Should OpenClaw core own the host-fenced final-capture journal and closure-evidence contract now, before the RFC establishes the permanent lifecycle, retention, repair, and migration owner?
rationale: The branch deliberately introduces durable recovery state and a trust boundary that cannot be resolved mechanically from tests or a private command alone.

options.title: Defer until RFC ownership is accepted
options.body: Keep the stacked PRs open, require current-head proof, and merge only after maintainers accept the permanent core-versus-host lifecycle boundary.

options.title: Accept the private core foundation
options.body: Approve the hidden capture and journal contract as the intended core foundation, then review the predecessor and restore/admission follow-up as one coordinated lifecycle.

recommendation.title: Defer until RFC ownership is accepted
recommendation.body: Keep the stacked PRs open, require current-head proof, and merge only after maintainers accept the permanent core-versus-host lifecycle boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed recovery-stack and RFC-context participant in the supplied review data; a repository owner must still make the final product decision.
